stories.headline: ARC-AGI-3 Launches as Interactive Benchmark, Frontier LLMs Score Below 1%

key_facts.fact: ARC-AGI-3 launched on March 25, 2026 as a fundamentally new benchmark that abandons static grid puzzles for interactive, video-game-like environments where AI agents must discover rules and solve problems with zero instructions.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-3, launched just yesterday on March 25, 2026, represents the most radical transformation of the ARC benchmark since François Chollet introduced it in 2019 — abandoning static grid puzzles entirely in favor of interactive, video-game-like environments where AI agents must discover rules, set goals, and solve problems with zero instructions.

key_facts.fact: Frontier LLMs including GPT-5 and Claude score below 1%, while simple CNN and graph-search approaches reach 12.58%, with human performance at 100%.
key_facts.excerpt: Early preview results: frontier LLMs like GPT-5 and Claude score below 1%, while simple CNN and graph-search approaches reach 12.58%. The gap between human performance (100%) and the best AI agent remains enormous.

key_facts.fact: The competition carries over $2 million in prizes across three tracks, with $700K grand prize for a 100% score and submissions due November 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The competition carries over $2 million in prizes across three tracks.

key_facts.fact: The benchmark contains 1,000+ levels across 150+ handcrafted environments, where agents enter 64x64 grid worlds with 16 colors and must learn through trial-and-error.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark contains '1,000+ levels across 150+ handcrafted environments.'

key_facts.fact: ARC-AGI-3 measures intelligence across time, not just final answers, capturing planning horizons, memory compression, and the ability to update beliefs as new evidence appears.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-3 makes that gap measurable by testing intelligence across time, not just final answers—capturing planning horizons, memory compression, and the ability to update beliefs as new evidence appears.

stories.headline: Google Introduces TurboQuant: 6x LLM Memory Reduction and 8x Speedup at Zero Accuracy Loss

key_facts.fact: Google Research published TurboQuant, a data-oblivious quantization framework that compresses LLM key-value caches to 3 bits per value, reducing memory by 6x and delivering up to 8x speedup with no accuracy loss.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Research has developed three compression algorithms: TurboQuant, PolarQuant, and Quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss (QJL). All three are designed to compress those caches aggressively without degrading model output quality.

key_facts.fact: TurboQuant combines PolarQuant, which converts Cartesian vectors to polar coordinates eliminating normalization overhead, with QJL which reduces residual errors to single sign bits with zero memory overhead.
key_facts.excerpt: PolarQuant handles the primary compression step by converting standard Cartesian coordinate vectors into polar coordinates. A conventional quantizer rec... TurboQuant addresses this by combining two underlying methods.

key_facts.fact: The algorithm was tested on Gemma and Mistral models running on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, achieving up to 8x performance boost over unquantized keys.
key_facts.excerpt: TurboQuant addresses this by combining two underlying methods. PolarQuant handles the primary compression step...

key_facts.fact: TurboQuant is data-oblivious, requiring no dataset-specific calibration for deployment, and was validated across LongBench, Needle In A Haystack, ZeroSCROLLS, RULER, and L-Eval benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: The persistent limitation of conventional approaches is that they require storing quantization constants in high precision for every small block of data, adding between one and two extra bits per number.

key_facts.fact: The compression enables powerful AI models to run locally on consumer devices like a 16GB Mac Mini or smartphones, according to coverage.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's TurboQuant reduces AI LLM cache memory capacity requirements by at least six times — up to 8x performance boost on Nvidia H100 GPUs, compresses KV caches to 3 bits with no accuracy loss

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Auto Mode for Claude Code, Letting AI Make Permission Decisions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released auto mode for Claude Code on March 24, 2026 as a research preview, placing it between babysitting every action and the risky --dangerously-skip-permissions flag.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's new 'auto mode,' now in research preview — meaning it's available for testing but not yet a finished product — is its latest attempt to thread that needle.

key_facts.fact: A built-in classifier reviews each tool call before execution, scanning for mass file deletions, data exfiltration attempts, malicious code execution, and prompt injection, blocking risky actions automatically.
key_facts.excerpt: Auto mode uses AI safeguards to review each action before it runs, checking for risky behavior the user didn't request and for signs of prompt injection... Any safe actions will proceed automatically, while the risky ones get blocked.

key_facts.fact: The feature is available now for Team plan users with rollout to Enterprise and API users in coming days, and is compatible with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 models.
key_facts.excerpt: The feature is available now as a research preview for Team plan users, with rollout to Enterprise and API users in coming days... Compatible with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 models.

key_facts.fact: Auto mode is disabled by default on the desktop app and requires admin settings for CLI and VS Code; Anthropic recommends use in isolated environments due to potential false positives.
key_facts.excerpt: Auto mode is disabled by default on desktop app and requires admin settings for CLI and VS Code. Anthropic recommends use in isolated environments due to potential false positives and negatives.

stories.headline: OpenAI Foundation Pledges $1B in Grants, Names Zaremba to Lead AI Resilience

key_facts.fact: The OpenAI Foundation committed to investing at least $1 billion in grants over the next year across four program areas: life sciences, jobs and economic impact, AI resilience, and community programs.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI on Tuesday announced key leadership appointments for its nonprofit arm and committed to investing at least $1 billion through the division over the next year in AI-related projects.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI co-founder Wojciech Zaremba is joining the Foundation to lead the AI Resilience program, and Robert Kaiden (ex-Deloitte, Twitter, Inspirato) joins as CFO.
key_facts.excerpt: Robert Kaiden was joining the foundation as CFO... OpenAI co-founder Wojciech Zaremba is joining the foundation to lead the company's...

key_facts.fact: The Foundation's spending represents a massive pivot: the nonprofit listed only $7.6 million in grants in 2024 and $3.3 million in expenses in 2019, making the $1B pledge a 130x increase.
key_facts.excerpt: IRS tax filings tell the story starkly: the nonprofit listed $51 million in expenses in 2018... and $3.3 million in 2019. In the most recent year it reported to the IRS, 2024, OpenAI's nonprofit received $4,433 in contributions and granted out $7.6 million.

key_facts.fact: Life sciences lead Jacob Trefethen previously oversaw $500M+ in grantmaking at Coefficient Giving; the program will target Alzheimer's research and high-mortality disease acceleration using AI-assisted drug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: Jacob Trefethen, newly hired as head of this pillar, previously oversaw more than $500 million in grantmaking at Coefficient Giving... His portfolio at the foundation will target Alzheimer's research, public health data infrastructure, and high-mortality disease acceleration using AI-assisted drug discovery.

key_facts.fact: The $1B is an early tranche of the $25 billion commitment the Foundation announced in October when OpenAI completed its recapitalization into a public benefit corporation valued at approximately $130 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: That $1 billion is framed as an early tranche of the $25 billion commitment the Foundation announced last October when OpenAI completed its recapitalisation.

stories.headline: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Steals SSH Keys and Cloud Credentials From 95M-Download Package

key_facts.fact: On March 24, 2026, LiteLLM PyPI versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published with credential-stealing malware via a compromised maintainer account, part of the broader TeamPCP supply chain campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 24, 2026, two PyPI releases of LiteLLM, 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, were published with malicious code as a result of a supply chain compromise.

key_facts.fact: The malicious .pth file auto-executed on every Python invocation without any import, stealing environment variables, SSH private keys, AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes credentials, git configs, shell history, and crypto wallet files.
key_facts.excerpt: Python automatically runs .pth files in your site-packages directory every time the Python interpreter starts. No import needed, no user interaction. The attacker hid a double base64-encoded payload inside this file.

key_facts.fact: LiteLLM has approximately 95 million monthly downloads on PyPI and serves as a dependency for major AI frameworks including DSPy and CrewAI, amplifying the attack's blast radius.
key_facts.excerpt: LiteLLM gets 97 million downloads per month... it has over 95 million monthly downloads on PyPI and serves as a universal API gateway for over 100 LLM providers.

key_facts.fact: Datadog's investigation traced the attack to a five-day TeamPCP campaign that began with the March 19 Trivy compromise, continued through CanisterWorm on npm, then hit Checkmarx KICS before reaching LiteLLM.
key_facts.excerpt: The LiteLLM compromise is the latest event in a five-day campaign that began with the March 19 Trivy compromise, continued with CanisterWorm on npm, and then reached Checkmarx KICS and related artifacts.

key_facts.fact: The attack was discovered accidentally when a developer's machine crashed from RAM exhaustion caused by a bug in the malware that triggered an exponential fork bomb.
key_facts.excerpt: Callum McMahon's machine crashes from RAM exhaustion - a bug in the malware caused an exponential fork bomb, leading to discovery

key_facts.fact: PyPI quarantined the entire litellm package and LiteLLM is pausing new releases until completing a broader supply-chain review.
key_facts.excerpt: We are pausing new LiteLLM releases until we complete a broader supply-chain review and confirm the release path is safe.

stories.headline: OpenAI Publishes Model Spec Philosophy, the 100-Page Framework Governing ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: On March 25, 2026, OpenAI published a detailed blog post explaining the philosophy and mechanics behind its Model Spec, the 100-page document that defines how ChatGPT should behave across all queries.
key_facts.excerpt: This post shares the backstory that is not in the Model Spec itself, including the philosophy and mechanics behind it: how it's structured, why we made those structural choices, and how we write, implement, and evolve it over time.

key_facts.fact: The Model Spec defines how models should follow instructions, resolve conflicts, respect user freedom, and behave safely, functioning both as a description of current behavior and a target for improvement.
key_facts.excerpt: The Model Spec is our formal framework for model behavior. It defines how we want models to follow instructions, resolve conflicts, respect user freedom, and behave safely across the incredibly broad range of queries that users ask them daily.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI frames the document as an interface so that researchers, policymakers, and the public can read, inspect, and debate intended model behavior rather than it being hidden inside the training process.
key_facts.excerpt: We use it to make intended behavior clearer, so we can train toward it, evaluate against it, and improve it over time.

stories.headline: Meta Reorganizes 1,000-Person Reality Labs Team Into AI-Native Pods

key_facts.fact: Meta Reality Labs is reorganizing a 1,000-employee developer tools team into AI-native pods, replacing traditional roles with three titles: AI Builder, AI Pod Lead, and AI Org Lead.
key_facts.excerpt: The memo described an overhaul of roles, titles, and team structures across a 1,000-employee team within Meta's Reality Labs... Everyone in the division will now have one of three titles: AI Builder, AI Pod Lead, or AI Org Lead.

key_facts.fact: The restructuring aims to create a flatter organization focused on engineering productivity and product quality, a structure that CEO Mark Zuckerberg has advocated.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our ultimate goal is to drive a step change in engineering productivity and product quality,' the memo reads.

key_facts.fact: Meta said the AI-native pod restructuring is unrelated to the approximately 700 layoffs it carried out on March 25 across Facebook, Global Operations, Recruiting, and other divisions.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta will lay off several hundred people across Reality Labs, social media, recruiting and sales on Wednesday (March 25).

key_facts.fact: The pod structure is part of Meta's broader AI-first push, which includes $115-135 billion in capital expenditure budgeted for 2026, primarily for AI servers and data center infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: For the current fiscal year, Meta has budgeted between $115 billion and $135 billion for investments, with the bulk earmarked for AI servers and data center infrastructure.

stories.headline: Figure AI Founder Launches Hark AI Lab With $100M and Apple's iPhone Air Designer

key_facts.fact: Brett Adcock, CEO of $39 billion humanoid robotics company Figure AI, publicly launched Hark with $100 million of his own money, hiring 45 engineers from Apple, Meta, Google, and Tesla.
key_facts.excerpt: Brett Adcock, the CEO of $39 billion humanoid robotics company Figure AI, publicly launched Hark on Tuesday, an AI lab he has been quietly funding with $100 million of his own money since late 2025. The San Jose company has 45 engineers and designers pulled from Apple, Meta, Google, and Tesla.

key_facts.fact: Hark's most notable hire is Abidur Chowdhury, the industrial designer who led Apple's iPhone Air team and presented the device at Apple's keynote, now serving as Director of Design.
key_facts.excerpt: Hark's most conspicuous hire is Abidur Chowdhury, the London-born industrial designer who led Apple's team on the iPhone Air and presented the device during Apple's keynote. Chowdhury left Apple last fall to join Adcock's lab as Director of Design.

key_facts.fact: Hark is building end-to-end speech, text, and vision models with persistent memory alongside custom AI hardware devices, planning to ship first AI models by summer 2026 and scale to 100 employees by mid-year.
key_facts.excerpt: Adcock plans to scale the team to 100 by mid-year and ship Hark's first AI models by summer. The company is building end-to-end speech, text, and vision models with what it calls 'highly personalized memory,' alongside a series of native hardware devices.

key_facts.fact: Chowdhury expressed skepticism about current AI wearables including pins and face-mounted cameras, saying Hark's philosophy centers on removing barriers between intelligence and users rather than adding gadgets.
key_facts.excerpt: He said he's 'not the biggest believer in a lot of the wearable AI platforms,' and called out pins and cameras strapped to faces as uncomfortable.

stories.headline: Anthropic Economic Index: Experienced AI Users Tackle Higher-Value Tasks With Better Success

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's March 2026 Economic Index report, studying Claude usage from February 5-12, found that high-tenure users (6+ months) demonstrate 4-5 percentage point higher conversation success rates than newer users.
key_facts.excerpt: We present evidence that high-tenure users have developed habits and strategies that allow them to better harness Claude's capabilities. Indeed, we document that more experienced users not only attempt higher-value tasks, but are also more likely to elicit successful responses.

key_facts.fact: Usage on Claude.ai diversified significantly: the top 10 tasks declined from 24% to 19% of conversations between November 2025 and February 2026, while personal use increased from 35% to 42%.
key_facts.excerpt: In Claude.ai, usage diversified, with the top 10 tasks accounting for a smaller share of usage last month than in November 2025.

key_facts.fact: The rate of augmentation (collaborative AI-human interaction) increased slightly in both Claude.ai and API traffic, continuing the trend that augmentation outpaces pure automation.
key_facts.excerpt: The rate of augmentation, collaborative interaction where the AI complements the user's abilities, increased slightly in both Claude.ai and API traffic.

key_facts.fact: For every $10 increase in hourly wage of the task, Opus model usage rises 1.5 percentage points on Claude.ai and 2.8 points on API, indicating users select more powerful models for higher-value work.
key_facts.excerpt: For every $10 hourly wage increase, Opus usage rises 1.5 percentage points on Claude.ai, 2.8 points on API.

stories.headline: Judge Says Pentagon's 'Supply Chain Risk' Designation Looks Like Attempt to 'Cripple' Anthropic

key_facts.fact: California District Judge Rita Lin stated on March 25 that the Defense Department's actions against Anthropic 'look like an attempt to cripple' the company, suggesting the designation may be illegal.
key_facts.excerpt: Judge Rita Lin stated on Tuesday that the Defense Department's actions 'look like an attempt to cripple Anthropic,' suggesting potential illegality in the Pentagon's approach.

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration had designated Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' for its stance on AI weapons regulation, specifically its insistence that AI products not be deployed for autonomous weapons or domestic surveillance without human oversight.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration had designated Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' for its stance on increased regulation, a move that would block the company from certain military contracts.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is the first US company to receive such a supply chain risk designation, which would cancel both direct government contracts and those of government contractors using Anthropic products.
key_facts.excerpt: This marks the first time a US company has received such a designation, entailing cancellation of government contracts and those of government contractors.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic challenged the ban as violating freedom of speech and due process rights, with the hearing indicating a potential preliminary injunction that could prevent billions in lost government contracts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic challenged the ban as violating freedom of speech and due process rights.
